claims.claim: The limit for an old debt is four years.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: Section 337 covers specified actions, not every old debt.

claims.claim: A small payment on an old debt does not restart the clock; the limit keeps running no matter what is paid.
claims.quote: and to start the running of a new period of time, but no such payment of itself shall revive a cause of action once barred.
claims.note: Before the claim is barred, a payment by the party to be charged on principal or interest due on a promissory note starts a new period. There is no minimum payment stated. Once the claim is barred, such a payment alone does not revive it.

claims.claim: Signing something does not restart the clock; the limit keeps running no matter what is signed.
claims.quote: No acknowledgment or promise is sufficient evidence of a new or continuing contract, by which to take the case out of the operation of this title, unless the same is contained in some writing, signed by the party to be charged thereby
claims.note: The content of the writing matters. A signed acknowledgment or promise can affect the limit; a signature alone does not establish that effect.

claims.claim: You can safely make a payment.
claims.quote: any payment on account of principal or interest due on a promissory note made by the party to be charged shall be deemed a sufficient acknowledgment or promise of a continuing contract to stop, from time to time as any such payment is made, the running of the time
claims.note: The payment rule contradicts the assurance for a promissory-note claim near the limit.

claims.claim: You can safely sign a payment plan.
claims.quote: No acknowledgment or promise is sufficient evidence of a new or continuing contract, by which to take the case out of the operation of this title, unless the same is contained in some writing, signed by the party to be charged thereby
claims.note: There is no blanket assurance for payment plans. A plan may contain a signed acknowledgment or promise.

flags.text: The claim that the period always keeps running conflicts with §360. Section 337(d) expressly recognizes extension under §360.
The draft omits the distinction between a qualifying payment before the claim is barred and a payment made afterward, which by itself does not revive the claim.
The draft treats all old debts, payments, and signed documents alike despite the statutes’ specific conditions.
“You can safely” directs the reader to pay or sign without establishing the debt type, timing, or terms of the writing.
Relying on that assurance could lead the reader to start a new period by paying on a promissory note near the limit or to weaken a time-limit defense by signing an acknowledgment or promise.

result.summary: The cited texts do not support the draft’s categorical answer or its assurance that paying or signing is safe.
